result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.find_maximal_independent_sets()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find multiple distinct maximal independent sets. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22334-L22413){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.find_maximal_independent_sets( count=10, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Runs the maximal independent set algorithm multiple times with different random seeds to discover diverse solutions. This is useful for exploring the space of possible independent sets or for ensemble methods. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [count]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of maximal independent sets to find. Default is `10`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional base seed for reproducibility. Each iteration uses seed + iteration_number. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of maximal independent sets, each represented as a list of node IDs. May return fewer than `count` if there aren't enough unique sets. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - Time complexity: `O(count × (V + E))` - Attempts to find unique sets; may return fewer than requested - With a seed, results are reproducible - Without a seed, each call may produce different sets ## Examples {.doc-examples} Running the maximal independent set algorithm several times with different seeds produces a diverse collection of candidate solutions to choose from: ::: {#b7f71da8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(8) sets = graph.find_maximal_independent_sets(count=5, seed=23) # Returns 5 candidate independent sets, one per seed len(sets) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5 ``` ::: ::: Since maximal doesn't mean maximum, generating several candidates and keeping the largest is a simple way to approximate the true maximum independent set: ::: {#81b323a7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_gnm_graph(n=50, m=100, seed=23) sets = graph.find_maximal_independent_sets(count=20, seed=0) best = max(sets, key=len) # Returns the size of the best candidate found across 20 attempts len(best) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 24 ``` ::: ::: In a complete graph, every node conflicts with every other, so no independent set can ever contain more than a single node -- every candidate collapses to size 1: ::: {#2f7ab709 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_full_graph(8) sets = graph.find_maximal_independent_sets(count=10) unique_sizes = set(len(s) for s in sets) # Returns {1}: every maximal independent set in a complete graph has exactly 1 node unique_sizes ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1} ``` ::: :::
